title: PR Explainer
summary: Explains a large pull request to a team — what changed, why, and how to explore it — from a diff and the repo it lands in.

page_types.purpose: Give a reader (live or async) a one-screen kickoff: what this artifact is, who should read which page, and how to ask questions.
Answer, in a few sentences, what changed and why — the one-screen version for someone who reads nothing else.
Show how the changed pieces fit into the system as a whole, before diving into any one of them.
Introduce each new or changed port/component: what it does, who calls it, and what it replaces.
Show real, generator-sourced payloads or command output proving the new behavior — never hand-typed.
Walk one real call through the system end to end: the call, the result, and who handles it next.
Compare old vs. new behavior (or option A vs. option B) cell by cell instead of in prose.
Show every changed file, bucketed by concern, generated fresh from the real diff — never hand-maintained.
Summarize what tests cover the change and what CI now checks, so a reviewer can trust the coverage claim.
Auto-built from contents.json's terms[] — every defined term in one place. Not hand-authored.
Auto-built from contents.json's sources[] and every <x-cite> used in the artifact. Not hand-authored.

default_sources.describe: The repo's grounding wiki, when one exists — commit-pinned notes already verified against the code
default_sources.hint: docs/wiki/INDEX.md first, then the notes it points to; skip when absent

default_sources.describe: The PR's changed files against its base branch
default_sources.hint: git diff / branch range — the primary source for a PR explainer

default_sources.describe: The repo checkout on the PR's own branch
default_sources.hint: modules, interfaces, configs, tests touched by the diff

options.description: Let the team explore and ask questions after merge

options.label: Document a big change
